annotation.kind: source selection, exact-tableau interpretation, complete Method 4s3pC order conditions, algorithm-linked local errors, explicit stability semantics, two global error regimes, and tier review

assumptions: An underlying exact four-stage Method 4s3pC tableau is supplied because the paper prints only rounded decimal coefficients; it has b^epsilon=0, satisfies all four exact consistency conditions through order three, and satisfies every exact simplified smooth condition (3.5a)-(3.5f).

Both branches consist of actual executions of the original additive Runge--Kutta algorithm (3.1), using the same exact tableau, operator pair, perturbation operator, epsilon, and chained computed and exact states.
The state is an arbitrary normed real vector space; the theorem does not select a dimension or norm for the paper.
The smooth branch is tagged well-behaved and has local errors O(h^4)+O(epsilon*h^4); the nonsmooth branch is tagged not-well-behaved and has local errors O(h^4)+O(epsilon*h^3).

For each branch, epsilon is positive, step sizes are nonnegative, the number of steps times the step size is at most a fixed nonnegative horizon, and all local and stability constants are nonnegative.
Stability means each accumulated global scheme or perturbation contribution is bounded by one stability constant times the sum of the corresponding algorithm-linked local error norms.
The exact-real model adds no IEEE rounding mode, unit-roundoff formula, overflow, underflow, subnormal, NaN, infinity, or solver-failure semantics.

formal_statement.lean_header: theorem p18_t3_method4s3pc_global_error_regimes {State : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup State] [NormedSpace Real State] {iota : Type*} (method : P18Method4s3pCSourceModel) (smooth : P18StableMethod4s3pCBranch State iota method 4) (nonsmooth : P18StableMethod4s3pCBranch State iota method 3) (hsmooth : smooth.tauRegime = wellBehaved) (hnonsmooth : nonsmooth.tauRegime = notWellBehaved) : method has zero perturbation weights, exact third-order consistency, and every exact smooth order-three condition, and smooth.globalError is O(h^3)+O(epsilon*h^3), and nonsmooth.globalError is O(h^3)+O(epsilon*h^2)
formal_statement.plain_language: For stable, algorithm-linked Method 4s3pC families, the scheme contribution is globally third order in both cases; the perturbation contribution is globally third order when tau is well-behaved and second order otherwise. The complete exact coefficient conditions used by the source remain visible.

informal_proof: Retain the exact tableau's zero perturbation weights and complete order-condition records. For each asymptotic parameter, sum the local scheme bounds and use stability to bound the global scheme contribution. Replace the finite sum by N times its uniform local bound, use N*h <= T, and obtain a hidden global constant times h^3. Repeat for the perturbation contribution: local epsilon*h^4 yields global epsilon*h^3 in the well-behaved branch, while local epsilon*h^3 yields global epsilon*h^2 in the other branch. Package the two contributions separately with existential constants.
informal_statement: Method 4s3pC's two stability-conditional page-18 global error regimes, retaining the complete exact third-order and smooth perturbation conditions and deriving the one-power local-to-global loss for actual additive Runge--Kutta executions.
